name: Baka (Cameroon)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Baka (Cameroon) is not in the catalog. All three stress-title hits attached to baka1272 by Glottolog are computerized keyword misassignments (lgcode 'computerized assignment from \"harry\"' for the two book reviews by Hyman & Wilson 1991 and Wei 2019; 'from \"ideal\"' for Revithiadou 1999, a dissertation on Greek/Russian/Salish lexical accent). None concerns Baka; priority none for all. The only Baka-specific prosody statement read (Djoupee 2001 §7.f.2, PDF p. 50) says loanword stress from French/English is mapped onto Baka tones, i.e. it is silent on native word stress; Djoupee 2017 §2.3 describes a three-tone lexical system with no mention of stress. Still unread and the best candidates for an explicit statement: Phillips 1981 'A phonology of Baka' (SIL Yaoundé, Cloudflare-blocked), Kilian-Hatz 1995 §2.1.3 'Töne und Intonation' (print only; TOC on file) / Kilian-Hatz 2000 English grammar (SIL). Saved: the three Glottolog reference records  and a sweep section appended to

new_statements.quote: Le ɓaka comprend les tons ponctuels et des suites mélodiques. [...] les verbes (359 termes), compte tenu du fait qu'ils ne portent pas de tons lexicaux sont exclus de l'analyse [p. 53] [...] Le corpus fait ressortir l'existence de trois tons phonétiques ponctuels: le ton haut (H) avec 507 occurrences, le ton bas (B) avec 829 occurrences et le ton moyen (M) avec 40 occurrences. Ils doivent leur statut phonologique à 29 oppositions [...] [p. 54] Comme les phonèmes consonantiques et vocaliques, les tons exercent une fonction distinctive. Ils exercent aussi une fonction grammaticale [p. 55]
new_statements.translation: Ɓaka has level tones and melodic sequences. [...] the verbs (359 items), given that they carry no lexical tones, are excluded from the analysis. [...] The corpus shows the existence of three phonetic level tones: high (H) with 507 occurrences, low (B) with 829 occurrences and mid (M) with 40 occurrences. They owe their phonological status to 29 oppositions [...] Like the consonant and vowel phonemes, the tones have a distinctive function. They also have a grammatical function.
new_statements.citation: Djoupee, Bertille. 2017. Description du ɓaka, une langue oubanguienne du Cameroun. Thèse de doctorat, INALCO / Université Sorbonne Paris Cité (NNT 2017USPCF034). Chapter 2 'Phonologie', §2.3 'Les tons'.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: opened (360 pp., HAL tel-01801763) with extracted text on PDF pp. 74-76 (= printed pp. 53-55). All three quoted segments are there verbatim: p. 53 §2.3 "Le ɓaka comprend les tons ponctuels et des suites mélodiques. En excluant de l'analyse les termes... les verbes (359 termes), compte tenu du fait qu'ils ne portent pas de tons lexicaux sont exclus de l'analyse, il reste une base de 1052..."; p. 54 §2.3.1 "Le corpus fait ressortir l'existence de trois tons phonétiques ponctuels: le ton haut (H) avec 507 occurrences, le ton bas (B) avec 829 occurrences et le ton moyen (M) avec 40 occurrences. Ils doivent leur statut phonologique à 29 oppositions (avec 9 incluant le ton moyen)..."…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Baka is a three-tone register language (H, L, marginal M; only open CV syllables; nouns carry lexical tone, verbs do not). The most authoritative modern description (Djoupee 2017) and the earlier MA thesis (Djoupee 2001, following Phillips 1981) treat tone as the only word-prosodic system and make no statement at all about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tone: mid tone is rare (39-40 lexical items), verbs have no lexical tone, tone sandhi in nominal morphology (Djoupee 2001).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical (word-level) tone analysis on a 1423-item lexicon of citation forms; no phrase-level stress or intonation statement.
new_statements.identity_note: Djoupee 2017 describes the Baka of the Haut-Nyong department, East Region, Cameroon (baka1272 proper; ISO bkc), from a spontaneous-speech corpus; Djoupee 2001 is the same Cameroon variety. Paulin 2010 (not opened) covers the Gabon (Minvoul) Baka. Glottolog's Rénaud 1976 entry is a misassignment (Bajele/Gyele, a Bantu language of Bipindi, not Baka).

new_statements.quote: Au niveau suprasegmental. Sur le plan prosodique, l'accent tonique de la langue source correspond aux tons ci-après: -Ton haut (anglais) ma'chine [misini]; (français) pa'paye [papaye]; -Ton bas (français) café [kapi] café; (anglais) cup-board [kʌbɔ:] armoire
new_statements.translation: At the suprasegmental level. On the prosodic plane, the word stress of the source language corresponds to the following tones: High tone: (English) ma'chine [misini]; (French) pa'paye [papaye]; Low tone: (French) café [kapi]; (English) cup-board [kʌbɔ:] 'cupboard'
new_statements.citation: Djoupee, Bertille. 2001. Morphologie nominale du Baka. Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé I. 103 pp.
new_statements.locator: §7.f.2 'Au niveau suprasegmental', PDF p. 50 of 103 (loanword phonology; no printed page number on the scan)
new_statements.reading: Weak, indirect evidence only: in French/English loans the source-language stress is re-interpreted as lexical tone, consistent with Baka being a tone language without a word-stress system. Djoupee 2017 (thesis, §2.3 pp. 53-55, already on file) describes three lexical tones (H/B/M) and never mentions stress or accent; Kilian-Hatz 1995 has a section 'Töne und Intonation' (§2.1.3, TOC only on file). No first-hand source read in this sweep states a word-stress position for Baka, and none of the three sweep items concerns Baka at all.

sources.note: Ch. 2 Phonologie (pp. 18-63) covers syllable structure (only open CV syllables, CVCV canonical), phonemes and tones: three level tones H/B/M with distinctive and grammatical function, verbs carry no lexical tone; the words accent/stress/intensité/proéminence never occur except 'accent aigu/grave' as tone diacritic names — silent on stress.
